house_main.name: otto's front room
house_main.description: low ceiling, one window onto the lane, a stove in the corner that he is proud of.

house_back.name: the back room
house_back.description: where he sleeps. bigger than it was, with the bed under the cold wall, a shelf, and a shutter on the window that has never quite closed.

lane_top.name: top of the lane
lane_top.description: cobbles, a drain he does not trust, his own front door on one side.

lane_bottom.name: bottom of the lane
lane_bottom.description: where the lane gives up and turns into grass. a bench too big for him.

shop_general.name: the general shop
shop_general.description: food, mostly. smells of paper bags.

shop_oddments.name: oddments
shop_oddments.description: everything that is not food. nothing is labelled. nobody is ever behind the counter.

post_office.name: the post office
post_office.description: one counter, a wall of small brass boxes. things from caleb arrive here.

library.name: the library
library.description: one room, colder than it should be, a shelf that caleb keeps putting things on.

orchard.name: the orchard
orchard.description: four old pear trees in a row, further apart than they look from the lane. the ground is soft with fallen fruit and the wasps are busy.

restaurant.name: the eating house
restaurant.description: three tables, a counter, and a kitchen you can hear but not see. warm in a way the lane never is. you have to pay.

yard.name: the yard behind his house
yard.description: soil, a leaf pile he has been adding to, and the back wall of his own house. his, in a way the lane is not. a gate in the hedge, into the orchard.

hedge.name: under the hedge
hedge.description: a low green tunnel running the length of the gardens. dark, dry, full of small noises. nothing bigger than him can get in here.

river.name: the river
river.description: it runs the whole length of the back of the houses and keeps going both ways. wider than the stream and slower. the shallow end at the top is barely over your head and the bottom end is not.

river_bank.name: the river walk
river_bank.description: a made path along the water, flagstones laid end to end the whole length of it, with benches set back off it and a lamp every so often on a cast post. somebody planted the beds and somebody still weeds them. at dusk the lamps come up the colour of an ember and the water goes the same colour back.

kitchen.name: the kitchen
kitchen.label: the kitchen
kitchen.description: narrow, warmer than the front room when the slab is going, and it smells of whatever was last on it. one small window, high up.

washroom.name: the washroom
washroom.label: the washroom
washroom.description: the cold end of the house. stone underfoot, a drip you cannot find, and the wall at the far end has something flat and shining set into it.

tip.name: the tip
tip.description: where the village puts what it has finished with. a low heap, gone through by rain. things in it are not yours or anyone's.

lane_out.name: the way out of the village
lane_out.description: a track going away from the village, between hedges, uphill.

found.how: looked properly at a gap in the top corner

church.name: the church
church.description: a tower with a spire on it, and a long low part behind. the door is shut. you can see it from a long way off.

found.how: looked properly at something standing up above the trees

back_lane.name: the back lane
back_lane.description: a narrow way behind the houses, hedge on one side and the backs of things on the other. nobody sweeps it.

cafe.name: the internet cafe
cafe.description: one room off the back lane. three tables, and on each one a machine. the light in here is the wrong colour and there is a sound under everything.

wharf_lane.name: down to the water
wharf_lane.description: a cut between two walls that drops away south, going down the whole way. you can smell the water before you can see it, and under that, tar.

wharf_row.name: wharf row
wharf_row.description: a long flat street with the working side of the village on it. everything here is open at the front so you can see the work happening, and all of it is louder than the lane.

wharf_w1.name: the boatyard
wharf_w1.description: a shed with no front wall and a boat upside down in the middle of it, bigger than your house. shavings up to your chin in the corners.

wharf_w3.name: the sawmill
wharf_w3.description: the loudest building there is. a blade under a table turns wood into two pieces of wood and sawdust hangs in the light like weather.

wharf_w4.name: the bath house
wharf_w4.description: hot inside, and so full of steam that the far wall is a rumour. the floor is wet stone and everything echoes twice.

wharf_w5.name: the glasshouse
wharf_w5.description: a building made mostly of windows, warm as a pocket, with more green things in it than the orchard. the air is wet and smells of soil.

wharf.name: the wharf
wharf.description: flat stone right out to the edge, and then the river, moving past faster than you expect. there is no rail. you keep well back and then you do not.

town_road.name: market row
town_road.description: a street with shops down both sides and more people on it in one morning than the lane sees in a month. nobody here knows your name, which is strange and not entirely bad.

town_square.name: the square
town_square.description: an open square of flagstones with a pump in the middle of it and buildings taller than anything at home standing round all four sides.

town_t1.name: the ironmonger
town_t1.description: dark, and every wall is drawers. whatever you are making, the part you need is in one of these drawers and the man knows which.

town_t2.name: the printer
town_t2.description: ink, hot metal and paper. a machine the size of a cart comes down on a sheet, lifts off, and the sheet has words on it.

town_t3.name: the clockmaker
town_t3.description: small, quiet, and ticking from every direction at slightly different times. there are more wheels in this one room than in the whole village.

town_t4.name: the music shop
town_t4.description: instruments hung up by their necks like washing. somebody is always half playing something in the back and stopping before the end.

town_t5.name: the bakery
town_t5.description: the warmest doorway in the world. you can stand in it for a long time before anyone minds.

town_t6.name: the market hall
town_t6.description: a roof on stone legs with nothing between them, so the weather comes through but the rain does not. trestles stacked against the end wall.

station.name: the station
station.description: a long platform under an iron canopy, tiled in diamonds, with a roof that curves over and a row of columns holding it up that have ironwork spreading out of the top of them like fans. there is a clock on a bracket over the edge and a bigger one up the tower, and both of them are right. standing at the platform is one wooden carriage, varnished, with its windows still in it. there is no engine. there has not been an engine for a long time.

woods_new.name: the woods
woods_new.description: proper trees, close together, and the light goes green and goes quiet. the ground is all needles and gives slightly under you.

station_road.name: the station road
station_road.description: the way out of the village, going on. past the church it stops being the way out of anywhere and becomes the way to one thing only. worn down the middle, a lamp at each end, and at the far end of it an archway through the middle of a building, with the platform straight through that.

objects.name: the range
objects.note: long, black and heavier than the house. two plates on the hot end, three doors, and a fire you can see through a little window in the middle one. the flue goes straight up through the ceiling. it is the best thing you own.

objects.name: a chair with a woven seat
objects.note: turned legs, four spindles up the back and a curved top rail worn pale where you lean on it. the seat is woven out of reed in four triangles that meet in the middle. it creaks and holds.

objects.name: a work table
objects.note: plank top, one drawer, and scored all over from things you have done on it.

objects.name: his bed
objects.note: leaves, a blanket, done properly.

objects.name: a shelf
objects.note: empty at the moment.

objects.name: the shelf
objects.note: whatever caleb has put there.

objects.name: the first pear tree
objects.note: the oldest. leans south. the fruit at the top is always best and always out of reach.

objects.name: the second pear tree
objects.note: straight, and younger. a branch comes low enough to matter.

objects.name: the third pear tree
objects.note: half dead on one side, loaded on the other.

objects.name: the fourth pear tree
objects.note: the one nearest the wall. windfalls collect against it.

objects.name: fallen pears in the grass
objects.note: bruised, warm from the ground, and sweeter than anything in the shop.

objects.name: the old wall
objects.note: brick, mostly. one part has come down and nobody has put it back.

objects.name: the counter
objects.note: too high for you by a long way. there is a step someone has left.

objects.name: a table by the stove
objects.note: the warmest seat in the lane.

objects.name: a hot supper
objects.note: whatever is on. it costs two coins and it is worth it.

objects.name: the kitchen stove
objects.note: you cannot see it. you can feel it through the wall.

objects.name: a pile of leaves
objects.note: dry at the bottom, damp on top. good for a nest if he wanted one.

objects.name: a cracked flowerpot on its side
objects.note: the crack goes most of the way round.

objects.name: a scatter of twigs
objects.note: different thicknesses. some snap, some bend.

objects.name: the hedge roots
objects.note: woven together over years into something like a low roof.

objects.name: old snail shells
objects.note: empty. curved, light, surprisingly stiff.

objects.name: reeds at the pond edge
objects.note: hollow all the way down, and straight.

objects.name: a flat stone at the water's edge
objects.note: holds the day's heat longer than anything else here.

objects.name: loose stones on the bank
objects.note: flat ones, round ones, one almost square.

objects.name: a plant you do not know
objects.note: himalayan balsam. soft green stem, pink hooded flower like a helmet. its seed pods burst when touched and throw seeds up to seven metres. sweet nectar under the leaf stems.

objects.name: a wedge of hard cheese
objects.note: keeps for weeks. he has never bought it.

objects.name: a pot of glue
objects.note: smells strongly. the brush is stuck to the lid.

objects.name: a coil of thin wire
objects.note: bends and stays bent.

objects.name: a small wool coat
objects.note: made for something about your size, which is a strange thought. carry it and the cold takes longer to get in.

objects.name: sheets of card
objects.note: stiffer than paper. cuts straight.

objects.name: the shallows at the top end
objects.note: gravel underfoot and the water moving over it. you can stand up in this bit.

objects.name: the deep pool
objects.note: dark green and you cannot see the bottom. you have not been in this bit.

objects.name: four stepping stones
objects.note: someone put them here a long time ago. the third one is missing and the gap is too wide.

objects.name: a bed of reeds
objects.note: taller than the pond ones and hollow all the way down.

objects.name: driftwood caught on the bend
objects.note: smooth, light, and already the right sort of shape for things.

objects.name: the backs of the shops
objects.note: nobody paints this side. there is a drainpipe you could climb if you were braver.

objects.name: the verge
objects.note: the strip of grass between the path and the backs of the shops, mown but not fussed over. this is where the path stops being a path.

objects.name: a bowl of leek soup
objects.note: on today. it comes out hot and they put it down in front of you.

objects.name: treacle tart
objects.note: on today. it comes out hot and they put it down in front of you.

objects.name: a flat iron slab over a firebox
objects.note: black, heavy, and cold most of the time. there is a hatch underneath for wood. it takes a long while to come up to heat and a long while to lose it.

objects.name: a shallow stone sink
objects.note: worn into a dip in the middle. the tap above it is stiff and the water comes in coughs, very cold.

objects.name: a shelf of jars
objects.note: most of them are empty and clean. two or three have something in that you have not opened. the lids are on tight.

objects.name: one heavy pan on a hook
objects.note: bigger than your head. the handle is long enough that you can use both paws.

objects.name: the nightstand
objects.note: just big enough for whatever you are still thinking about when you lie down. there is a ring on it from something wet.

objects.name: a tin bath much too big for you
objects.note: you could lie down in it twice over. it rings when you knock it. filling it would take a great many jugs.

objects.name: a white jug with a chip out of the lip
objects.note: heavier than it looks when it is full.

objects.name: something flat set into the wall
objects.note: cold, flat, and held in a wooden frame. there is another washroom in it, the same as this one but turned the wrong way round, and when you move, something small and dark and spiked moves in there too, at exactly the same moment. it will not do anything you do not do first.

objects.name: a coil of thin wire
objects.note: springy. it holds a bend if you make it sharp enough.

objects.name: a small spring
objects.note: pushes back when you squash it, and keeps doing it.

objects.name: a flattened tin
objects.note: thin metal, bright where the rain has not got at it.

objects.name: a piece of thick glass
objects.note: edges gone smooth. things look bent through it.

objects.name: a clock that has stopped
objects.note: a case, a face, and a lot of small parts behind it.

objects.name: a strip of brass
objects.note: heavier than it looks and it does not rust.

objects.name: a handful of corks
objects.note: light, and they squeeze.

objects.name: a small grey bar
objects.note: it sticks to the tin and not to the cork.

objects.name: a wooden box on a post
objects.note: open at the top, with a slot in the lid. there is nothing in it. whatever is left in it does not stay left.

objects.name: a gap in the top corner
objects.note: the hedge stops and starts again, and the grass between is worn flat.

objects.name: something standing up above the trees
objects.note: too far to make out. it is taller than it is wide and it comes to a point.

objects.name: a dark line along the top of the field
objects.note: trees, closer together than the ones in the orchard, and no light between them.

objects.name: a machine with a face that lights up
objects.note: the face is cold white and it is not warm to touch. things move on it when you press the board in front of it.

objects.name: a flat board covered in little squares
objects.note: every square has a mark on it. pressing one puts that mark on the lit face.

objects.name: a smooth lump on a cord
objects.note: it slides. when it slides, an arrow on the lit face slides the same way.

objects.name: a second machine, its face dark
objects.note: the same as the lit one but nothing on it. there is a switch underneath.

objects.name: the counter
objects.note: nobody behind it, same as everywhere. a bowl with coins in it and a card saying what an hour costs.

objects.name: a sound under everything
objects.note: low, and it does not stop. you feel it in the table more than you hear it.

objects.name: a path worn through the grass
objects.note: the grass is flattened in a line going off south between two walls, the way grass goes when the same feet do the same thing for years. something down there is worth walking to.

objects.name: a milestone
objects.note: a squat stone with a flat face and a number cut into it, leaning the way everything old leans. the number is how far it is to somewhere, and the somewhere is further up this road.

objects.name: a board on the lych gate
objects.note: a wooden board with paper under glass, gone brown, listing times in two columns. there is a road going on past the church, and whatever these times are for is up it.

objects.name: offcuts of planking
objects.note: ends of boards sawn off and stacked against the wall, because nobody here throws wood away. some are longer than you are.

objects.name: a tub of pitch
objects.note: black, sticky, and it smells like a road in summer. it goes on the outside of a hull so the water stays on the outside too. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: the saw bench
objects.note: a long table with a slot down the middle and a blade standing up through it. the blade is not turning. you are glad the blade is not turning.

objects.name: a heap of sawdust
objects.note: dry, soft, and warmer than the floor. you could sleep in this very happily if it were not somebody's sawdust.

objects.name: a bundle of battens
objects.note: thin square sticks, all cut the same length and tied with twine. the most useful shape there is. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: the hot tap
objects.note: brass, and stiff, and it goes if you lean your whole weight on it. what comes out is hot enough to make the room vanish.

objects.name: a slatted bench
objects.note: slats worn pale and smooth by people sitting on them wet. it is the warmest thing to sit on anywhere.

objects.name: a stack of glass panes
objects.note: flat, cold, sharp at the edges, and the room looks slightly wrong through them. you would have to be careful with these. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: trays of seedlings
objects.note: hundreds of them in shallow trays, every single one leaning the same way, towards the light.

objects.name: the mooring rings
objects.note: iron hoops set into the stone edge, rubbed bright on the inside where ropes have pulled on them. nothing is tied to any of them now.

objects.name: the old crane
objects.note: a timber post with an arm across the top and a chain hanging off the end. you can push it round and it goes, slowly, complaining the whole way.

objects.name: a tray of nails
objects.note: sorted by length into wooden compartments. there are more sizes of nail in this tray than you knew there were sizes of anything. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: a coil of soft wire
objects.note: grey and soft, wound on a wooden spool. it bends where you bend it and then it stays bent. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: the vice
objects.note: bolted to the end of the counter. you turn the handle and it holds whatever is in its jaws harder than you could hold anything.

objects.name: the press
objects.note: iron, and taller than the man working it. it comes down on a sheet with a sound you feel through the floor. he lets it down slowly when he notices you watching.

objects.name: a ream of paper
objects.note: white sheets cut square and stacked, more than you could cover in a year of writing. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: a tin of ink
objects.note: thick black stuff, not runny the way you expected. it goes onto the roller, never onto the paper. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: a tray of brass gears
objects.note: wheels with teeth round the edge, every one a different size, lying loose in a tray like coins. they are made to turn each other. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: a mainspring
objects.note: a flat ribbon of steel wound tight into a drum. it wants to come undone, and it will, for days, if it is let out slowly enough. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: the clock on the wall
objects.note: a tall case with a weight swinging in it. it is the only thing in the town that is never wrong.

objects.name: a tin whistle
objects.note: a metal tube with six holes down it. you can get a noise out of it straight away and a tune out of it eventually. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: a card of wound strings
objects.note: wire wound on a paper card. they are sold to be played, but they are also simply very good string. it is behind the counter, and nobody has said a price. you could stand and look at it for a while, which is what you do.

objects.name: the day's loaves
objects.note: still warm underneath. the crust ticks quietly while it cools.

objects.name: trestles stacked against the wall
objects.note: folding wooden legs, dozens of them, leaning in a stack. on a market morning they are tables and the rest of the week they are this.

objects.name: a rope handrail
objects.note: a rope through iron eyes down one wall, because the slope is steep enough that people have wanted something to hold. it is tarred and it comes off on your paws.

objects.name: barrels under a tarpaulin
objects.note: a row of them against the wall with a sheet pulled over the top and tied down. whatever is in them, it is the smell of the whole street.

objects.name: a lamp on a bracket
objects.note: out from the wall on an iron arm, high up out of the way of the work. it is lit before it needs to be, every day.

objects.name: stalls along the kerb
objects.note: trestle tables with awnings over them, pulled out across the front of the shops, selling what the shop behind does not. you have to walk round them.

objects.name: a gutter running the length of it
objects.note: a stone channel at the edge with water going along it faster than the river does. things float in it. you could race something down this.

objects.name: the pump
objects.note: iron, waist-high on a person, with a curved handle and a worn stone trough under the spout. it takes both your shoulders and then the water comes.

objects.name: the notice board
objects.note: a glass case on legs with papers pinned behind it, layered over each other, the old ones gone yellow underneath the new. things that have happened and things that are going to.

objects.name: a fallen trunk
objects.note: down across the slope and going soft, with bark coming off in sheets. there is a whole other world living under the bark and you can lift it and look.

objects.name: deadfall branches
objects.note: dry sticks all over the floor in every length there is, free, and nobody wants them. this is the best place in the world if you are building something.

objects.name: fungi on the north side
objects.note: growing in steps up the shaded side of the trunks, and they are not the same two weeks running. some are the colour of nothing else here.

objects.name: the needle floor
objects.note: inches of dropped needles, dry underneath, and it gives under you and springs back. you can hear yourself walking on it and nothing else.

objects.name: the drain
objects.note: an iron grating in the low point of the lane with a hole under it that goes further down than you can see. things go in and do not come back.

objects.name: stacked crates
objects.note: behind the backs of the shops, slatted wooden boxes stacked higher than you, some broken. the broken ones are nobody's.

objects.name: a lamp post
objects.note: a cast post with a glass case on top of it. at dusk something in it comes up slowly the colour of an ember, and then the water has one of these in it too, wobbling.

objects.name: a lamp post
objects.note: a cast post with a glass case on top of it. at dusk something in it comes up slowly the colour of an ember, and then the water has one of these in it too, wobbling.

objects.name: a lamp post
objects.note: a cast post with a glass case on top of it. at dusk something in it comes up slowly the colour of an ember, and then the water has one of these in it too, wobbling.

objects.name: a lamp post
objects.note: a cast post with a glass case on top of it. at dusk something in it comes up slowly the colour of an ember, and then the water has one of these in it too, wobbling.

objects.name: a bench facing the water
objects.note: iron ends and wooden slats, set back off the path so your feet do not get walked over. it faces the river and nothing else.

objects.name: a bench facing the water
objects.note: iron ends and wooden slats, set back off the path so your feet do not get walked over. it faces the river and nothing else.

objects.name: a bench facing the water
objects.note: iron ends and wooden slats, set back off the path so your feet do not get walked over. it faces the river and nothing else.

objects.name: a planted bed
objects.note: a long bed cut into the grass on the path side, planted in rows and weeded by somebody who has not given up. there is something out in every month of the year, which cannot be an accident.

objects.name: a planted bed
objects.note: a long bed cut into the grass on the path side, planted in rows and weeded by somebody who has not given up. there is something out in every month of the year, which cannot be an accident.

objects.name: a lamp on the station road
objects.note: the same cast post as the ones on the river walk. somebody still lights this road, for the people who would be coming up it.

objects.name: a lamp on the station road
objects.note: the same cast post as the ones on the river walk. somebody still lights this road, for the people who would be coming up it.

objects.name: the carriage
objects.note: wooden, and varnished so dark it is nearly red. ten tall windows down the side with smaller ones above them, a roof that rises in the middle into a second little roof with its own windows, and an open platform at each end with a curved rail round it and steps down to the ballast. there is a wheel on a stand at one end for the brake. nothing is coupled to it and nothing ever will be.

objects.name: the clock on the tower
objects.note: white face, black hands, four of them so it can be read from anywhere. it has not stopped.

objects.name: the clock over the platform edge
objects.note: hung off a bracket so it faces both ways down the platform, for people who are not here.

objects.name: a bench on the platform
objects.note: cast ends and wooden slats, looking at the rails. somebody sat here a long time ago waiting for this.

objects.name: a letter on top of the box
objects.note: one sheet, weighted down with a stone, in a hand that slopes. it says: THIS BOX IS HOW IT WORKS HERE. put a thing you have made through the slot and leave it. do not wait about. somebody will want it, and somebody will leave what they think it was worth, and that is what you will find in the bottom next time you look. a thing that actually works is worth more than a thing that only looks like it. nobody checks and nobody is watching. it has gone on like this for longer than anyone remembers.

objects.name: plank
objects.note: came in the post.

objects.name: something leaning against the end wall
objects.note: two rings, taller than you, one behind the other, held apart by a frame of thin bars. there are two seats along the top, one in front of the other, and two sets of bent handles. the rings turn when you push them and the whole thing wants to fall over. it is cold and it has been rained on. you have no idea what it is, what it is for, or who left it here.
